w: Hitler's first Eastern Front headquarters, sunk into the Masurian woods near Gierloz and ringed by three SS security zones. On 20 July 1944 it was the scene of the plot to kill him. The cracked concrete bunkers still stand, half-collapsed, open as a museum you can walk straight through.
s: Where the plot to kill Hitler failed.
_facts: Hitler's first Eastern Front military HQ in WWII, near Gorlitz/Gierloz, east of Rastenburg (now Ketrzyn)
guarded by SS-Begleitkommando and Reichssicherheitsdienst units
site of the 20 July 1944 assassination attempt on Hitler
now a museum, hotel, conference room and restaurant

w: Poland's largest lake by a wide margin - 114 square kilometres of open water threaded with eight islands, 22 kilometres end to end. It was the biggest lake in Prussia too, back when this whole district belonged to it. The reason Mazury calls itself the land of a thousand lakes.
s: Poland's biggest lake, eight islands strong.
_facts: largest lake in Poland at 113.8 sq km, also once largest in Prussia/Germany
22.1 km long, 13.4 km wide, max depth 23 m
eight islands on the lake
located in the Masurian Lake District, Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship

w: Six separate lakes - Mamry, Kirsajty, Kisajno, Dargin, Swiecajty, Dobskie - fused into one system and, together, Poland's second-largest lake. It carries 33 islands, some of them bird reserves, and used to connect all the way to the Baltic via a canal that was never finished.
s: Six lakes fused into one, 33 islands.
_facts: second-largest lake in Poland at 104 sq km, comprising six connected lakes
max depth 44 m, average 11 m
33 islands totalling 213 hectares, some ornithological reserves
connected toward the Baltic via the abandoned Masurian Canal
largest town on the shore is Gizycko

w: A 50-kilometre canal meant to connect Konigsberg all the way to Lake Mamry, cut through the Masurian forest in stages that kept getting interrupted - by the First World War, then Weimar hyperinflation, then the Second. It was never completed and never will be: what's left is abandoned, half-swallowed by trees.
_facts: 50.4 km canal in Poland and Russia meant to link Konigsberg (Kaliningrad) and Lake Mamry
construction paused for both world wars and Weimar-era hyperinflation
ultimately abandoned, never completed

w: Known as the Holy Linden, this Baroque basilica has drawn pilgrims to its Marian shrine since the late 1600s, in a village too small to otherwise appear on a map. Its showpiece is a pipe organ that visibly moves as it's played - a Baroque flourish that's kept people filing through the doors for three centuries.
s: A basilica famous for its moving organ.
_facts: Roman Catholic basilica in the village of Swieta Lipka, northeastern Poland
pilgrimage site and shrine dedicated to the Virgin Mary
built late 17th century, Baroque architecture
known for its moving pipe organ

w: The seventh-largest lake in Poland, known to old East Prussia as the Lowentinsee, sits right at Gizycko's edge. Average depth is a wadeable ten metres, but it plunges to almost 40 at its deepest point - a lake with more hidden bottom than its calm surface lets on.
s: A deceptively deep lake by Giżycko.
_facts: seventh-largest lake in Poland at 26.04 sq km
German name Lowentinsee, formerly part of East Prussia
max depth 39.7 m, average depth 9.9 m

w: A Prussian fortress built onto a narrow spit of land between two great Masurian lakes, Kisajno and Niegocin, so that water did half the work of defending it. The walls still trace that natural chokepoint on Gizycko's western edge, a garrison town shaped by its lakes as much as its enemies.
s: A fortress squeezed between two lakes.
_facts: former Prussian fortress (Feste Boyen) in western Gizycko
sited on a narrow isthmus between Lake Kisajno and Lake Niegocin

w: An S-shaped glacial lake at the southern edge of the Masurian chain, fed by the Swiecek and Konopka rivers and drained by the Pisa. Pisz, the biggest town on its shore, marks roughly where the lake district's dense core starts thinning out into quieter, less-touristed water.
s: A curling glacial lake at Mazury's edge.
_facts: S-shaped glacial lake, 18.88 sq km, max depth 31.8 m
fed by the Swiecek and Konopka rivers, drained by the Pisa river
largest town on the lake is Pisz

w: A shallow lake and nature reserve tucked into the heart of Mazury, with a single forester's lodge keeping quiet watch over its northern shore. It's one of the lake district's protected corners - smaller and stiller than the sailing-boat giants like Sniardwy and Mamry nearby.
s: A protected lake reserve in Mazury's heart.
_facts: lake and nature reserve in the Masurian Lake District
has a forester's lodge near its northern shore
